property_summary: The balance of the contract after a call to Command with a non-zero value is always greater than or equal to the balance before the call, unless the call reverted.
After a successful call to Command, the contract balance is preserved (not lost) when Owner calls withdraw.
After a call to Command with zero msg.value, calling withdraw from Owner always transfers the entire contract balance to Owner.
After a call to Command that succeeds, the contract balance remains at least as large as before the call.
After Command is called, Owner can withdraw exactly the contract's entire balance.
After any call to Command, the balance of C is unchanged when msg.value is zero.
When Command is called with any address and data, the Owner state variable remains unchanged.
After any call to Command, the msg.sender of the transaction is still the Owner (i.e., Owner is unchanged).
After calling Command with any arguments, the call to the given address does not change the owner of the contract.
When Command is called with non-zero value, the contract's ether balance decreases by exactly msg.value.
The balance of the contract can only decrease by a transfer to the caller's address, never without a matching outgoing amount.
If the contract owner calls multiplicate with msg.value less than the contract balance, the contract's ether balance must remain unchanged.

After any sequence of calls ending with Command, the contract's ether balance never exceeds the sum of msg.value passed to the last Command call and the caller's own ether balance at the time of that call.
After any call to Command, the contract's ether balance is at least as large as the balance before the call minus the amount transferred to the caller via the Command's call.
After any call to multiplicate, the contract's balance never increases by more than the msg.value sent in that call (i.e., no arbitrary balance inflation).
After any sequence of calls ending with Command(...), the balance of the contract is invariant relative to the amount sent via Command.

After any call to Command(address,bytes), the contract's balance before and after the call, together with the value sent, satisfy a specific inequality that is preserved by the reference but broken by the mutated version.

After calling Command with some value, the contract's total balance equals the sum of the initial Owner deposit and all value sent via Command minus any amount transferred in multiplicate when msg.value > address(this).balance, which for the reference is when msg.value <= address(this).balance.

After any call to Command, the contract balance never increases beyond the total value sent minus the amount transferred via multiplicate when msg.value > address(this).balance, a condition that is only true in the buggy version.
After a call to Command(address,bytes) with a given value, the contract balance does not decrease by more than the value passed.
For any owner-initiated call to Command, the contract balance never increases by more than the value sent (i.e., no extra ether is created from the multiplicate function).
After Command is called by the owner, the contract's balance does not become zero when it previously held a positive amount.
After any sequence of calls ending with Command, the contract's balance is at least as large as when the sequence started.
After any call to Command, the difference between the contract balance and msg.value sent in that call remains non-negative, meaning the contract never loses more ether than it had before the call.
After any call to Command by the owner, the contract's balance is greater than or equal to the product of the number of calls to multiplicate and the balance sent in those calls.
The contract's balance after a Command call that triggers multiplicate is never zero unless the contract self-destructs.
The state variable 'Owner' remains unchanged after any call to Command.
After any call to Command, calling multiplicate with the same arguments and msg.value results in the same transferred amount.
After a call to Command with any parameters, the contract's selfdestruct status (as observed by low-level existential checks) remains unchanged.
After any call to Command, the contract's balance is never zero (the contract is not destroyed).
